demoFields.hint: Printed at the top of the death certificate. If the death was never registered, get it registered first — the pension cannot be sanctioned without it.

demoFields.label: Date of Birth / Age of Applicant (completed years)
demoFields.hint: You must be 40 or above. Write the date exactly as it stands on the age proof attached.

demoFields.label: Whether Remarried
demoFields.hint: The pension is only for a widow who has not remarried, and it stops from the month of remarriage.

demoFields.label: Full Postal Address
demoFields.value: Chandanpur, Post Mahua, Block Mahua, Dist. Vaishali, Bihar – 844122
demoFields.hint: Village or ward, post office, block, district and PIN. Give the address where you live now, even if the ration card shows the husband's village.

demoFields.label: Category (SC / ST / OBC / General)
demoFields.hint: Tick one — several states sanction against category-wise quotas.

demoFields.label: BPL Family Identification No. / Ration Card No.
demoFields.hint: Copy from the BPL ration card. If the card is still in the husband's name, say so here and attach it anyway.

demoFields.label: Number of Dependent Children, with ages
demoFields.hint: Some states pay an additional child allowance on top, so fill this even when the form marks it optional.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number
demoFields.hint: All twelve digits, of the widow herself — not the late husband's.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: The sanction message and every monthly credit are sent to this number.

demoFields.label: Bank / Post Office Account (bank, branch, account no., IFSC)
demoFields.value: Punjab National Bank, Mahua Branch, A/c 40987654321, IFSC PUNB0099000
demoFields.hint: The account must be in the widow's own name and single-operated. A joint account with a son is routinely rejected.

demoFields.label: Name of Nominee and Relationship
demoFields.hint: Who receives unpaid arrears. A minor nominee needs a guardian's name written beside it.

demoFields.label: Signature / Thumb Impression of Applicant, with place and date
demoFields.value: L.T.I. of Sunita Devi Yadav, Chandanpur, 22-09-2026
demoFields.hint: A thumb impression is as valid as a signature, but it must be attested by the Sarpanch or a Gazetted Officer.

demoFields.label: Verification / Recommendation by Gram Panchayat (for office use)
demoFields.value: Certified that the applicant is a widow residing in this Gram Panchayat, has not remarried, and belongs to a BPL family. — Mukhiya, Chandanpur Gram Panchayat (round seal)
demoFields.hint: Leave it blank for the Mukhiya, Sarpanch or Ward Member. The words 'has not remarried' must appear in this certificate.

demoSteps: Register the husband's death first if that was never done — the Registrar of Births and Deaths at the Panchayat or municipal office issues the certificate, and the whole pension file rests on it. Get two extra certified copies while you are there.

Collect the blank NSAP widow pension form free of charge from the Gram Panchayat clerk, the Block Development Office, the municipal ward office or a Common Service Centre; it can also be printed from the NSAP site on plain A4.

Fill it in ink, in block letters. Copy the husband's name, the date of death and the registration number letter by letter from the death certificate, because the verifying officer compares the two documents side by side.

Open a single-name savings account in the widow's own name if there is not one already, and seed it with Aadhaar at the branch. A joint account or the late husband's account will hold up the payment even after sanction.
Attach the death certificate, age proof, BPL ration card, Aadhaar photocopy, passbook first page and two photographs. Paste one photograph on the form and clip the other to the file.

Take the form to the Sarpanch, Mukhiya or Ward Member to sign and stamp the verification block, making sure the certificate states that she has not remarried — a verification without those words is sent back.
Submit it at the Gram Panchayat office and ask for the case to be placed before the next Gram Sabha, which approves the beneficiary list before the Block office acts on it.
Demand a dated acknowledgement carrying an inward number. Failing that, get your own acknowledgement line stamped and signed on a photocopy of the form and keep it safe.

Sanction by the Block Development Officer normally takes 30 to 60 days after the Gram Sabha approves the name, and the first credit usually includes arrears from the month of sanction. After three months of silence, send a written reminder quoting the inward number and then an RTI application (Rs.10) to the BDO.
schemes.helpline: Block Development Office; the district Social Welfare Officer's number is displayed on the Gram Panchayat notice board

schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (formerly IGNOAPS)
schemes.department: Ministry of Rural Development — Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP)
schemes.brief: A monthly pension for people aged 60 and above who belong to a below-poverty-line household. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly the National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP); the amount and rules stay the same. The Centre pays a fixed share and almost every state adds a top-up, so the amount that actually reaches the bank account is usually larger than the central figure.
schemes.benefit: Rs.200/month (Rs.500 after age 80) from the Centre, plus the state top-up
eligibility: Age 60 years or more on the date of application
Household is on the state's below-poverty-line (BPL) list
Not drawing a government service pension or another social-security pension
Indian citizen, resident of the village or ward where the form is submitted
documents: Age proof — Aadhaar, birth certificate, school leaving certificate or voter ID
BPL ration card, or the family's serial number on the BPL list
Aadhaar card photocopy
First page of the bank or post-office passbook (account in the applicant's own name)
Two passport-size photographs
Residence proof — voter ID, ration card or Panchayat certificate
schemes.submitAt: Gram Panchayat office, or the Block Development Office (BDO); in a town, the municipal ward office

demoFields.label: Name of the Applicant
demoFields.hint: Spell it exactly as it appears on the Aadhaar card, in block letters. A spelling mismatch is the commonest reason a sanctioned pension never reaches the account.

demoFields.label: Father's / Husband's Name
demoFields.hint: Husband's name for a married or widowed woman, father's name otherwise.

demoFields.label: Date of Birth / Age (completed years)
demoFields.hint: You must be 60 or above on the day you apply. Write the date exactly as it stands on the age proof you are attaching.

demoFields.label: Sex
demoFields.hint: Tick one box: Male / Female / Transgender.

demoFields.label: Full Postal Address
demoFields.value: House No. 44, Kherwadi, Post Ambegaon, Tal. Shirur, Dist. Pune, Maharashtra – 412210
demoFields.hint: Village or ward, post office, block or taluka, district and PIN — complete enough for the postman to find you.

demoFields.label: Category (SC / ST / OBC / General)
demoFields.hint: Tick one. Several states sanction pensions against category-wise quotas, so a blank box can delay the file.

demoFields.label: BPL Family Identification No. / Ration Card No.
demoFields.hint: Copy it from the BPL ration card. If the family is on the BPL list but holds no card, write its serial number on that list.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number
demoFields.hint: All twelve digits. The pension is credited to the Aadhaar-seeded account, so this must match the bank record.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: A number somebody actually answers — the sanction and every credit are announced by SMS.

demoFields.label: Bank / Post Office Account (bank, branch, account no., IFSC)
demoFields.value: Bank of Maharashtra, Shirur Branch, A/c 60123456789, IFSC MAHB0000999
demoFields.hint: The account must be in the applicant's own name, not a son's or daughter's. Copy all four items from the first page of the passbook.

demoFields.label: Name of Nominee and Relationship
demoFields.hint: Who should receive the arrears if you die before they are paid. Add the nominee's address if the form asks for it.

demoFields.label: Whether in receipt of any other pension
demoFields.hint: Answer truthfully — it is cross-checked against the state pension database, and a false answer cancels the sanction and recovers the money.

demoFields.label: Signature / Thumb Impression of Applicant, with place and date
demoFields.value: L.T.I. of Shantabai P. Gaikwad, Kherwadi, 22-09-2026
demoFields.hint: If you cannot sign, a left thumb impression is fully valid. It has to be attested by the Sarpanch or any Gazetted Officer.

demoFields.label: Verification / Recommendation by Gram Panchayat (for office use)
demoFields.value: Certified that the applicant resides in this Gram Panchayat and belongs to a BPL family. — Sarpanch, Kherwadi Gram Panchayat (round seal)
demoFields.hint: Leave this block empty. The Sarpanch or Ward Member fills, signs and stamps it — never write in it yourself.

demoSteps: Ask the Gram Panchayat clerk for the blank NSAP old-age pension form (in a town, the municipal ward office or the Block Development Office). The form is free — nobody may charge for it. The same form is stocked at the Common Service Centre and can be printed on plain A4 from the NSAP site.

Fill it in ballpoint ink, in block letters, and in the language the office works in. Do not leave a box blank — write 'NIL' or 'Not applicable' instead, because a blank box lets the file be returned as incomplete.

Settle the age box first, since it decides the case: attach Aadhaar, or a birth or school-leaving certificate, or a voter ID. If no paper carries the year of birth, the Medical Officer at the Primary Health Centre can issue an age certificate free of charge.

Attach a photocopy of the BPL ration card, the first page of the passbook, the Aadhaar photocopy and two photographs. Paste one photograph on the form and clip the second one to it; sign across the pasted photo if the form has a signature line running over it.

Take the filled form to the Sarpanch or Ward Member to sign and stamp the verification block at the bottom. In a municipality the Ward Councillor or the Commissioner's clerk signs instead. This attestation is not optional — an unverified form is not put up to the Gram Sabha.

Hand the form in at the Gram Panchayat office and ask the clerk to list it in the next Gram Sabha agenda, because the Gram Sabha approves the beneficiary list before the Block office sanctions anything.

Demand a dated acknowledgement with an inward number written on it. If the clerk will not give one, put your own acknowledgement line on a photocopy of the form and have it stamped and signed there and then — that photocopy is your proof of the date.

The Gram Sabha resolution travels to the Block Development Officer, who sanctions the pension (in some states the Tehsildar or Sub-Divisional Officer signs). Expect 30 to 60 days; the first credit often carries arrears from the month of sanction.

If nothing has arrived in three months, file a written reminder at the Block office quoting the inward number, and follow it with an RTI application (Rs.10) to the BDO asking for the status of that application and the date of the sanction order.
schemes.helpline: Block Development Office; the district Social Welfare Officer's number is displayed on the Gram Panchayat notice board

schemes.title: DAY-NRLM Self-Help Group (Aajeevika SHG / Lakhpati Didi)
schemes.department: Ministry of Rural Development — Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission, through each State Rural Livelihoods Mission
schemes.brief: Women from poor village families join a self-help group (SHG) of 10 to 20 women who save a small sum every week and lend to each other. A group that runs well gets a Revolving Fund of Rs.20,000–30,000, can borrow up to Rs.2.5 lakh from the Community Investment Fund through its village federation, and gets bank loans without collateral at a low rate. Members are trained and supported to take up dairy, farming or small businesses, with the aim of earning Rs.1 lakh a year as a 'Lakhpati Didi'. About 10 crore women are in these groups; you join through your village organisation or the block office of your state's livelihood mission, such as JEEViKA in Bihar, UMED in Maharashtra or Kudumbashree in Kerala.
schemes.benefit: Revolving Fund Rs.20,000–30,000 per group, up to Rs.2.5 lakh CIF per group, bank loans at 7% up to Rs.3 lakh
eligibility: Women from poor rural households, picked out by the village itself or from the SECC deprivation list
One woman from each household, in one group
A group has 10 to 20 members (fewer in hilly or remote areas and in groups of persons with disabilities)
The group must meet, save, lend, repay on time and keep books regularly (the 'Panchasutra') to get the Revolving Fund
Community Investment Fund and bank loans follow once the group is graded by the mission and the bank
Lakhpati Didi support usually goes to members who have been in an SHG for at least two years and have used the CIF
documents: Aadhaar card of each member
Passport-size photographs of the members
Savings account opened in the group's name, with a resolution signed by all members
ID proof of the three office-bearers who will operate the group account
Bank passbook of each member
Group meeting register and savings and loan ledger, kept by the group's bookkeeper
schemes.submitAt: Speak to the Community Resource Person (CRP, the SHG didi or sakhi) or the Village Organisation in your village, or go to the Block Mission Management Unit of your State Rural Livelihoods Mission at the block office. Join an existing group or form a new one with 10–20 women from nearby households; the CRP helps open the group's bank account at the nearest branch and enters the group in the mission's records. Take your Aadhaar, photographs and bank passbook.

demoFields.hint: The name the members agree on at the first meeting.

demoFields.hint: As on Aadhaar.

demoFields.hint: From Aadhaar or another age proof.

demoFields.hint: SC, ST, OBC, General or Minority.

demoSteps: Meet the CRP or Village Organisation. With 10–20 women from nearby poor households, hold the first meeting, name the group and fix the weekly saving.
Open a savings account in the group's name with the three office-bearers as signatories; the CRP records the group and each member with the mission.
Meet every week, save, lend among yourselves, repay on time and keep the books for about three months.
The group gets the Revolving Fund of Rs.20,000–30,000 in its account and joins the Village Organisation.
Through the village federation the group can borrow from the Community Investment Fund, up to Rs.2.5 lakh per SHG, against the members' credit plan.
The bank gives the group loans without collateral, at 7% for loans up to Rs.3 lakh, with bigger loans after each repayment. Members use them for dairy, farming, shops or other work.
Members are trained under the Lakhpati Didi plan, and the CRP records household income in the Digital Aajeevika Register.

schemes.title: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
schemes.department: National Health Mission, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
schemes.brief: Cash given to a mother who delivers her baby in a government hospital, or in an approved private hospital if she is from a BPL, SC or ST family. The village ASHA helps you register, takes you for check-ups and gets the payment made. Under a separate scheme (JSSK) the delivery itself is free, even a caesarean, along with medicines, food and the ambulance. JSY money is extra, paid into your bank account after the delivery.
schemes.benefit: Rs.1,400 (village) or Rs.1,000 (town) in low-performing states; Rs.700 or Rs.600 elsewhere
eligibility: In Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Assam, Uttarakhand and Jammu & Kashmir: every pregnant woman who delivers in a government hospital or health centre
In all other states: women from BPL, SC or ST families who deliver in a government hospital or health centre
In every state: BPL, SC or ST women who deliver in an approved (accredited) private hospital
There is no age limit and no limit on the number of children for a hospital delivery
BPL women who deliver at home get Rs.500
documents: Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card or JSY card given at registration
Aadhaar card of the mother
Bank account passbook in the mother's name, linked to Aadhaar
BPL ration card, or SC/ST caste certificate (needed outside the low-performing states, and for a private hospital delivery)
Discharge slip or delivery record from the hospital
Mobile number
schemes.submitAt: At the government hospital or health centre where you deliver: before going home, hand your MCP card, Aadhaar copy, bank passbook copy and (where needed) the BPL ration card or caste certificate to the JSY desk or labour-room staff. Your village ASHA can collect and submit them for you. For a home delivery, give them to the ASHA or the ANM at the sub-centre.

demoSteps: As soon as you know you are pregnant, tell the village ASHA or go to the sub-centre. The ANM registers you and gives you the MCP card.
Go for the pregnancy check-ups written on the card. Ask for the BPL or caste certificate to be noted if you live outside the low-performing states.
When labour starts, call 102 or 108 for the free ambulance and go to a government hospital or health centre with the MCP card.
Before leaving the hospital, give your Aadhaar, bank passbook copy and MCP card to the JSY desk or labour-room staff, or hand them to the ASHA.
The hospital enters your claim. The money is sent straight to your bank account, usually within a few weeks.
If it has not come in a month, ask the ASHA or the hospital's JSY clerk, or call 104 with your MCP card number.

schemes.title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY / Sukanya Account)
schemes.department: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance; run through India Post and authorised banks
schemes.brief: A savings account in a girl's name that pays one of the highest safe interest rates in the country, 8.2% a year for October to December 2026, completely tax-free. A parent opens it before the girl turns 10, at a post office or authorised bank, with as little as Rs.250, and keeps depositing for 15 years; the account matures 21 years after opening. Half the money can be taken out after she turns 18 for her studies. Rs.1,000 a month for 15 years grows to about Rs.5.5 lakh at today's rate.
schemes.benefit: 8.2% tax-free interest; deposit Rs.250 to Rs.1.5 lakh a year
eligibility: Girl child below 10 years of age, resident in India
Opened by the girl's parent or legal guardian; accounts opened by grandparents must be moved to a parent's name
One account per girl, and at most two girls per family (a third only for twins or triplets)
Minimum Rs.250 and maximum Rs.1.5 lakh in a financial year, paid for 15 years from opening
A year without the minimum deposit can be made good by paying Rs.250 for that year plus Rs.50 penalty
documents: Account opening form with Sukanya Samriddhi Account ticked
Girl's birth certificate
Parent's Aadhaar card
Parent's PAN card, or Form 60 if you have no PAN
Passport-size photos of the parent (and of the girl where the office asks)
Address proof, if the address on Aadhaar is different
First deposit of at least Rs.250, in cash or by cheque
schemes.submitAt: Any post office with a savings bank counter, or a branch of an authorised bank such as SBI, Punjab National Bank, Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank or ICICI Bank. Take the filled form, the girl's birth certificate, your Aadhaar and PAN with originals for checking, two photos and the first deposit of at least Rs.250; the passbook is handed to you at the counter.

demoFields.label: Name of Post Office
demoFields.hint: The post office or bank branch where you are opening the account. It can be moved to any other place in India later.

demoFields.label: Type of account
demoFields.hint: The same form is used for every post office savings scheme, so tick SSA.

demoFields.label: Name of account holder (girl)
demoFields.hint: The girl's name exactly as written on her birth certificate.

demoFields.label: Date of birth of the girl
demoFields.hint: She must be under 10 on the day the account is opened.

demoFields.label: Name of guardian and relation
demoFields.hint: The parent who will run the account until the girl turns 18.

demoFields.label: Guardian's Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar of the parent filling the form; show the original at the counter.

demoFields.label: Guardian's PAN
demoFields.hint: If you do not have a PAN, write Form 60 and fill that form instead.

demoFields.label: Mobile number and address
demoFields.hint: Messages about deposits and interest come to this number.

demoFields.label: Amount of first deposit
demoFields.hint: At least Rs.250. Later deposits can be any amount in multiples of Rs.50, up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year.

demoSteps: Take the account opening form at the post office counter, or download it from the India Post forms page, and tick Sukanya Samriddhi Account.
Fill in the girl's details from her birth certificate and your own as parent, and attach copies of the birth certificate, your Aadhaar and PAN, with photos.
Hand it in with the first deposit. The clerk checks the originals and gives you a passbook with the account number.
Deposit at least Rs.250 every financial year for 15 years, at the counter, through the India Post or IPPB app, or by standing instruction.
Interest, 8.2% for October to December 2026 and revised every quarter, is added every 31 March and is tax-free. Deposits also count under section 80C in the old tax regime.
When she turns 18 or passes Class 10, up to half of the balance can be withdrawn for higher studies with the admission letter or fee slip.
At 21 years from opening, or at her marriage after 18, fill the closure form and the full amount is paid into her bank account.
schemes.helpline: 1800-266-6868 (India Post customer care); your bank branch if the account is with a bank

schemes.title: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi
schemes.department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
schemes.brief: Every land-holding farmer family gets Rs.6,000 a year from the central government, paid straight into the bank account. The money comes in three instalments of Rs.2,000, about four months apart. There is no fee and no middleman.
schemes.benefit: Rs.6,000 a year in 3 instalments
eligibility: The family owns cultivable land. A family means husband, wife and minor children, and gets one payment between them
The land record must be in the applicant's own name in the village revenue record
Aadhaar must be seeded in the bank account, and e-KYC must be completed on the portal
Not eligible: income-tax payers, serving or retired government employees (Class IV / Group D staff are still eligible), pensioners drawing Rs.10,000 or more a month
Not eligible: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects in practice, and holders of constitutional posts
Not eligible: institutional landholders, such as land held by a trust or company
documents: Aadhaar card, with mobile number linked for OTP
Land record (khatauni, khasra, RoR or 7/12 extract) showing the applicant's name
Bank passbook first page, showing account number and IFSC
Ration card or other proof of the family
Recent passport-size photograph

demoFields.label: Type of farmer
demoFields.hint: Choose Rural Farmer if your land is in a village panchayat, Urban Farmer if it falls inside a municipal area.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The 12 digits printed on your Aadhaar card. The mobile number linked to it will receive the OTP, so keep that phone with you.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: The number linked to your Aadhaar. Every message about your instalment comes to this number, so do not give someone else's phone.

demoFields.label: Name (exactly as on Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: Copy the spelling from the Aadhaar card letter by letter. If it does not match, the bank transfer will fail.

demoFields.label: Category
demoFields.hint: SC, ST, OBC or General, as written on your caste certificate. Choose General if you do not hold one.

Enter your Aadhaar number, mobile number and state, tick Rural or Urban farmer, and fill the captcha to get an OTP.
Type the OTP, then a second OTP sent by Aadhaar, so that your identity is verified.
Fill your name, category, bank account and IFSC exactly as they appear on your documents.
Add your land details, one row for each khasra or survey number, and upload the land record and your photo.
Save the form and note the registration number that appears on screen.
Your application now goes to the village revenue officer and then the state government for approval. Check Beneficiary Status on the same site using your Aadhaar number.
Once approved, complete e-KYC under Farmers Corner, else the instalment will be held back.

schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
schemes.department: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
schemes.brief: Crop insurance that pays the farmer when the harvest is lost to drought, flood, pests, hail or an unseasonal storm. The farmer pays only a small part of the premium, 2% of the sum insured for kharif crops and 1.5% for rabi, and the two governments pay the rest.
schemes.benefit: Premium of only 1.5% to 5%; full sum insured on crop loss
eligibility: Any farmer growing a notified crop in a notified area, whether the land is owned, leased or share-cropped
Enrolment is voluntary. Loanee farmers are covered through their bank unless they opt out in writing
A tenant or share-cropper must hold a written agreement or a sowing certificate from the village officer
The crop must be registered before the cut-off date for that season, usually 31 July for kharif and 31 December for rabi
The same plot cannot be insured twice, by the bank and by the farmer separately
documents: Aadhaar card
Bank passbook first page with account number and IFSC
Land record (7/12 extract, khatauni or RoR) for the insured plot
Sowing certificate or self-declaration of the crop sown
Tenancy agreement, if the land is taken on lease
Recent photograph of the sown field, useful when a claim is filed

demoFields.label: Season and year
demoFields.hint: Kharif is the monsoon sowing, rabi the winter one. Only the season open for enrolment can be picked.

demoFields.label: Farmer name (as on Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: The name of the person who will receive the claim money. Spell it as on the Aadhaar card.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: 12 digits from your Aadhaar card. An OTP comes to the mobile linked with it.

demoFields.label: Farmer type
demoFields.hint: Owner if the land is in your name, tenant or share-cropper if you farm someone else's land. A share-cropper must upload the agreement.

demoFields.label: State / District / Tehsil / Village
demoFields.hint: Choose the village where the field lies. Premium rates and notified crops change from village to village.

demoFields.hint: The account where the claim will land. The premium is also debited from it, so keep the balance ready.

Sign in and choose Insurance of Loanee or Non-Loanee farmer, whichever fits you.
Pick the season, year and scheme, then your state, district, tehsil and village.
Enter your Aadhaar, name and bank details, and verify the Aadhaar OTP.
Add the crop, the area sown in hectares, the sowing date and the survey number of the plot.
Upload the land record, and the tenancy paper if you farm someone else's land.
Check the premium the screen shows, pay it online, and save the policy receipt and application number.
If the crop is damaged later, report it within 72 hours on the Crop Insurance app or on 14447, and the surveyor will visit.

schemes.title: PM Mudra Yojana
schemes.department: Ministry of Finance
schemes.brief: A collateral-free loan for a small non-farm business, a shop, a workshop, a service or a small manufacturing unit, in steps: Shishu up to Rs.50,000, Kishore up to Rs.5 lakh, Tarun up to Rs.10 lakh, and Tarun Plus up to Rs.20 lakh for those who have repaid a Tarun loan. Jan Samarth checks your eligibility and gives an in-principle approval online, but the loan is sanctioned and paid out by the bank branch after it sees your original papers. You can also skip the portal and apply straight at any bank branch.
schemes.benefit: Loan up to Rs.20 Lakh, no collateral
eligibility: Any Indian citizen with a business plan or a running non-farm business: manufacturing, trading, services, or allied farm work such as dairy or poultry
Not for crop loans and not for large companies. This is for micro enterprises
No collateral, and no processing fee on Shishu loans
The business must be your own and the account must not be a defaulter with any bank
Tarun Plus, Rs.10 lakh to Rs.20 lakh, only for those who took a Tarun loan and repaid it in full
Many banks give women borrowers a concession on the interest rate
documents: Aadhaar Card
PAN Card
Passport size photos
Address proof and business proof such as rent agreement, licence or Udyam certificate
Quotation for the machinery or goods to be bought
Bank statement of last 6 months
Caste certificate, if applicable
Details of any existing loan

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: Jan Samarth logs you in with this number and an OTP.

demoFields.label: Applicant's Full Name
demoFields.hint: As on PAN and Aadhaar. Both are checked against each other.

demoFields.label: PAN Number
demoFields.hint: The portal pulls your name and eligibility from PAN.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number
demoFields.hint: For e-KYC. The branch will verify it again in person.

demoFields.label: Business Activity
demoFields.value: Tailoring unit with 3 machines, stitching school uniforms
demoFields.hint: Say plainly what you make or sell. Writing only Business is not enough for the bank.

demoFields.label: Years in Business
demoFields.hint: A brand new business also qualifies. Then give your plan instead of past sales.

demoFields.label: Annual Sales or Expected Turnover
demoFields.hint: Take it from your bank statement, or give an honest estimate for a new unit.

demoFields.label: Loan Amount Required
demoFields.hint: Match it to the quotation you will attach. Ask only for what you can repay.

demoFields.label: Loan Category
demoFields.hint: Shishu up to Rs.50,000, Kishore up to Rs.5 lakh, Tarun up to Rs.10 lakh.

demoFields.label: Bank and Branch Chosen
demoFields.value: Bank of Baroda, Raipur Pandri branch
demoFields.hint: Pick a branch you can visit. The branch where you already have an account is usually quickest.

demoSteps: On Jan Samarth choose the Business Activity Loan category, then Mudra.
Answer the short eligibility questions. The portal tells you at once whether you qualify.
Register with your mobile number and OTP, then PAN and Aadhaar e-KYC.
Fill in the business details, the amount you need and exactly what it will be spent on.
Submit and note the in-principle approval and its reference number. This is not yet the sanction.
Choose a lender from the list the portal shows you.
Visit that branch with the originals: Aadhaar, PAN, photos, address and business proof, quotations, and six months of bank statements.
The branch verifies everything and sanctions the loan. Ask for the sanction letter and the interest rate in writing.
The money comes as a transfer to your account, or as a Mudra card or overdraft for working capital.
You may skip the portal altogether and apply at any bank branch, regional rural bank, small finance bank, NBFC or MFI. No agent is needed and nobody should charge you a fee.

schemes.title: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor Loan)
schemes.department: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, with SIDBI
schemes.brief: A working-capital loan for street vendors with no collateral: Rs.15,000 first, then Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 once each loan is repaid. Repaying on time earns a 7% interest subsidy credited to your loan account, and taking and making payments by UPI or QR code earns cashback of up to Rs.1,600; vendors who repay the second loan can get a UPI-linked RuPay credit card. The scheme was restructured and extended in August 2025, and loans are given till 31 March 2030. You can apply yourself on the portal, or through a CSC or your municipal office.
schemes.benefit: Loans of Rs.15,000, Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 without collateral, with 7% interest subsidy
eligibility: Street vendor selling in a town or city, with a Certificate of Vending or ID card from the municipality or Town Vending Committee
Or named in the municipality's vendor survey (Survey Reference Number), even if no certificate was issued
Vendors left out of the survey, or from nearby villages and peri-urban areas who sell within town limits, can apply with a Letter of Recommendation (LoR) from the municipality
Without an LoR, you must be a member of a vendors' association or have received the one-time Covid assistance
The Rs.25,000 and Rs.50,000 loans are given only after the previous loan is fully repaid
documents: Aadhaar card, with your mobile number linked to it (needed for e-KYC)
Certificate of Vending or vendor ID card, or Survey Reference Number, or Letter of Recommendation
Savings bank account passbook
Passport-size photo
Proof of membership of a vendors' association, if you have no LoR

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: Your Aadhaar-linked mobile. Fill the captcha and tap Request OTP; the OTP comes here.

demoFields.label: Vendor category
demoFields.value: In the survey, no certificate issued
demoFields.hint: Pick the line that fits you: have a certificate or ID card, in the survey without one, have an LoR, or none of these.

demoFields.label: Survey Reference Number (SRN)
demoFields.hint: Find it with the survey status search on the portal. With a certificate, give its number; with an LoR, upload it.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Verified by OTP; your name, date of birth and address are taken from Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Father's / husband's name
demoFields.hint: As on your Aadhaar or vending certificate.

demoFields.label: Social category
demoFields.hint: General, SC, ST, OBC or minority, as you belong.

demoFields.label: Vending details
demoFields.value: Fixed spot, Lajpat Nagar market, New Delhi
demoFields.hint: Where you sell and whether you sit at one place or move with a cart.

demoFields.label: Goods sold
demoFields.hint: What you mainly sell, for example tea, snacks, clothes, flowers or repairs.

demoFields.label: Lender and branch
demoFields.hint: Choose the bank where you have your savings account; the loan is credited there.

demoFields.label: Loan amount
demoFields.hint: The first loan is Rs.15,000. Rs.25,000 and then Rs.50,000 follow after repayment.

demoSteps: Check your name in the vendor survey on the portal and keep your SRN, certificate or LoR ready. Make sure your mobile number is linked to Aadhaar.
Open the PM SVANidhi login page, enter your mobile number and captcha, and log in with the OTP. A CSC or your municipal office can do this for you.
Choose your vendor category, complete Aadhaar e-KYC, fill in your vending and bank details, and submit. Note the application number.
The municipality verifies you; if you have no certificate, it issues the Letter of Recommendation online.
The bank approves the application and credits Rs.15,000 to your account. Repay it in monthly instalments over 12 months.
For on-time repayment, the 7% interest subsidy is credited to your loan account every quarter. Use UPI or QR for sales to earn the cashback.
After repaying, use Apply for 25k (18 months) and then Apply for 50k (36 months) on the portal; after the second loan you can apply for the RuPay credit card.
schemes.helpline: 1800-11-1979 (PM SVANidhi toll-free) / pmsvanidhi.support@sidbi.in (technical help)

schemes.title: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.department: Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises
schemes.brief: For artisans and craftspeople in 18 traditional trades who work with their hands and tools: carpenters, blacksmiths, potters, tailors, barbers, cobblers, masons and others. You get a certificate and ID card, skill training with a stipend of Rs.500 a day, a Rs.15,000 toolkit voucher, and a collateral-free loan of Rs.1 lakh and then Rs.2 lakh at 5% interest. You cannot register yourself from home: registration is done at a Common Service Centre with a biometric Aadhaar check, and three committees verify you afterwards.
schemes.benefit: Rs.15,000 toolkit + Rs.3 Lakh loan at 5%
eligibility: Working with your hands and tools in one of the 18 listed trades, self-employed and in the unorganised sector
Aged 18 or above on the date of registration
The trade must be your present occupation and the same one you register for
Only one member of a family. Husband, wife and unmarried children count as one family
No credit-based loan taken under PMEGP, PM SVANidhi or Mudra in the last 5 years. A fully repaid Mudra loan does not block you
Government employees and their family members are not eligible
documents: Aadhaar Card
Mobile number linked to Aadhaar
Ration card, or Aadhaar of family members
Bank account number and IFSC
Caste certificate, where the state asks for it
Proof of the trade you practise

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number
demoFields.hint: The CSC operator takes your fingerprint against this, so carry the card itself.

demoFields.label: Full Name (as on Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: Any difference from Aadhaar and the biometric check will fail.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number Linked to Aadhaar
demoFields.hint: It must be the number registered with Aadhaar, not a newer one you use now.

demoFields.label: Date of Birth
demoFields.hint: You must be 18 or older on the day you register.

demoFields.label: Trade
demoFields.hint: Choose from the 18 trades listed. The toolkit voucher is fixed according to the trade.

demoFields.label: Family Details and Ration Card Number
demoFields.value: Wife and two children, ration card RJ-00-000123
demoFields.hint: Only one member of a family can take this benefit, so check nobody at home has already registered.

demoFields.label: Address, Gram Panchayat or Ward
demoFields.value: Village Kotra, Gram Panchayat Kotra, Barmer, Rajasthan
demoFields.hint: This panchayat or ward office does the first verification, so get the name exactly right.

demoFields.label: Place of Work
demoFields.hint: Home, a rented shop or a roadside stall are all accepted.

demoFields.label: Bank Account Number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: Stipend, toolkit voucher and loan all come through this account.

demoFields.label: Loan Taken Earlier Under PMEGP, SVANidhi or Mudra
demoFields.hint: Answer honestly. A Mudra loan you have fully repaid does not disqualify you.

demoSteps: Check on the portal that your trade is one of the 18 and that nobody else in the family has registered.
Go to the nearest Common Service Centre with your Aadhaar card and the mobile linked to it. This step cannot be done at home.
The CSC operator does the biometric Aadhaar check and fills the form. Sit beside them and check every entry before it is submitted.
Collect the acknowledgement and the application number. Registration at a CSC is free under this scheme.
Your gram panchayat or urban local body verifies you first.
The district implementation committee checks next, and then the screening committee approves.
Once approved, download the PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card from the portal.
Do the 5 to 7 day basic training. The Rs.500 a day stipend comes by DBT.
Claim the Rs.15,000 toolkit e-voucher after the basic training is over.
Apply at the bank for the first loan of Rs.1 lakh, repayable over 18 months. A second loan of Rs.2 lakh follows after you repay it and take the advanced training.
schemes.helpline: PM Vishwakarma toll-free 18002677777 and 17923

schemes.title: Udyam Registration (MSME)

GSTIN, if applicable
Bank account number and IFSC

schemes.title: Skill India Digital Hub (PMKVY Training)

schemes.title: PM Internship Scheme

You get Rs.5,000 a month and a one-time grant of Rs.6,000, and the government pays your PMJJBY and PMSBY insurance premium. You fill one profile and pick up to five internships; companies shortlist from that pool.

eligibility: Aged 21 to 24 years on the date you apply

Family income not above Rs.8 lakh in the last financial year

schemes.title: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY, First Job Rs.15,000)
schemes.department: Ministry of Labour & Employment, through EPFO
schemes.brief: A one-time payment of up to Rs.15,000 for people in their first PF-covered job: anyone who joins an EPFO-registered employer between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027, has never had PF deducted before, and earns up to Rs.1 lakh a month. There is no application form; the money comes from your employer's monthly PF filing, but only if your UAN was made with face authentication on the UMANG app and your bank account is seeded with Aadhaar. Half is paid after 6 months of work, and the rest after 12 months and a short online financial literacy course, kept in a savings deposit for a fixed period. It was announced in Budget 2024-25 as the Employment Linked Incentive (ELI) scheme.
schemes.benefit: Up to Rs.15,000 (one month's PF wage) in two instalments
eligibility: First job with PF: you were never a contributing EPF member before 1 August 2025
Joined an EPFO-registered employer between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027
Gross salary up to Rs.1 lakh a month at the time of joining
UAN generated or verified with face authentication on the UMANG app
Stay with the same employer for 6 completed months (first instalment) and 12 months (second instalment)
Bank account seeded with Aadhaar; until it is, the money is held back

Smartphone with the UMANG and AadhaarFaceRD apps for the face scan

Your UAN, given to the employer when you join

demoFields.hint: Type the OTP within the time shown on the screen.

demoFields.hint: Install AadhaarFaceRD from the Play Store first. Look straight at the camera in good light and blink when asked.

demoFields.hint: The money goes by Aadhaar to the account your Aadhaar is mapped to for DBT, which may not be the account in your PF record.

demoSteps: On your first job, make your UAN yourself in the UMANG app (EPFO > UAN Allotment and Activation) with Aadhaar, OTP and a face scan, and give the UAN to your employer.
Get your bank account seeded with Aadhaar for DBT at your branch. Without it the payment waits, though it keeps adding up.
Your employer files PF every month. Check in UMANG or on the EPFO member portal that your contributions are showing.
After 6 completed months with the same employer, the first instalment, half of one month's PF wage up to Rs.7,500, comes to your Aadhaar-seeded account.
Finish the free online financial literacy course on the EPFO portal before your 12th month.
After 12 completed months, the second instalment (the rest, total up to Rs.15,000) is put into a savings deposit in your name, to be paid out later.
If nothing arrives, call the EPFO help desk or file a grievance on EPFiGMS with your UAN.
