Open the graduation (Snatak) link, register with your university, college, roll number and date of birth, and confirm the OTP. The portal then sends a user ID and password by SMS.
Log in and fill the form — name exactly as on the marksheet, Aadhaar, and a bank account in your own name with the correct IFSC.
Upload the marksheet, Aadhaar and the bank passbook page as small PDFs. The portal caps the file size and simply refuses anything larger.
Submit, note the application number and print the acknowledgement.

Your college verifies the entry and the university forwards the list to the department. Check status and any rejection reason on the same portal — a wrong IFSC, a name mismatch or an inactive account are the usual ones, and they can be corrected and resubmitted.
Rs 50,000 is paid by direct transfer into your account once the sanction list is published. Watch the payment status page on Medhasoft until it shows paid.
schemes.helpline: The Kanya Utthan nodal teacher at your college, or the District Education Officer of your district

schemes.title: Chandigarh Old Age Pension
schemes.department: Department of Social Welfare, Women & Child Development, Chandigarh Administration
schemes.brief: A monthly pension for Chandigarh residents aged 60 and above whose family income is up to Rs.1.5 lakh a year. The UT pays Rs.1,000 a month, and with the central share the pensioner gets Rs.1,200, or Rs.1,500 from age 80. You apply at any Sampark centre, where the operator scans your documents and files the application online. The pension is paid every month into your Aadhaar-seeded bank account. About 18,600 people get it.
schemes.benefit: Rs.1,200 a month (Rs.1,500 from age 80), including the central share
eligibility: Age 60 years or above
Total family income not above Rs.1.5 lakh a year
Living in Chandigarh for more than 3 years
Not already getting another pension (the form asks for the amount and source if you do)
documents: Two passport-size photographs, one cross-signed on the form
Aadhaar card
Residence proof for the last three years (voter card, ration card, electricity bill, house allotment letter or residence certificate)
Date of birth proof (birth certificate, school leaving certificate, passport, PAN card or senior citizen card)
Income certificate from the competent authority
Mobile number and bank account details for the Aadhaar-seeded pension account
schemes.portalName: Social Welfare, Women & Child Development, Chandigarh
schemes.submitAt: Any Sampark centre in Chandigarh. Take the filled form with the cross-signed photograph, the signed self-undertaking and the Aadhaar consent page, plus the originals of your Aadhaar, three-year residence proof, age proof and income certificate. The operator checks and scans them and files the online application on the e-District system. If you have no birth proof, get your age certified first by the Principal Medical Officer at GMSH-16 or GMCH-32. For questions, go to the Department of Social Welfare, Additional Town Hall Building, 3rd Floor, Sector 17-C.

demoFields.label: Applicant's Name
demoFields.hint: The person in whose name the pension order will be issued.

demoFields.label: Father's / Husband's Name
demoFields.hint: As on your Aadhaar or voter card.

demoFields.label: Date of Birth / Age
demoFields.hint: Must be 60 or more. Attach the date of birth proof.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar No.
demoFields.hint: The pension is linked to this Aadhaar and paid to the account seeded with it.

demoFields.label: Mobile No.
demoFields.hint: SMS updates on your application come here.

demoFields.label: Gender
demoFields.hint: Tick Male, Female or Transgender.

demoFields.label: Belong to SC / OBC
demoFields.hint: Tick only if it applies to you.

demoFields.label: House No. / Sector or Village
demoFields.hint: Where you have lived for the last three years. It must match your residence proof.

demoFields.label: Present total family monthly income
demoFields.hint: Add up everyone's income. A year's total must not be above Rs.1.5 lakh.

demoFields.label: Whether in receipt of any pension
demoFields.hint: If Yes, write the monthly amount and who pays it.

demoSteps: Download the old age pension form, or take one at the Sampark centre, and fill in your details.
Paste the photograph, cross-sign it, and sign the self-undertaking and the Aadhaar consent page.
Go to a Sampark centre with the originals. The operator scans them, files your application online and gives you the application number.
The Social Welfare Department verifies the papers and sanctions the pension. Track it on the e-District status page with your application number.
The pension is paid every month into your Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
Give your life certificate to the department each year so the pension does not stop.
schemes.helpline: 0172-2700372 — Department of Social Welfare, Women & Child Development, Chandigarh; 181 — Women and Child Helpline

schemes.title: Chandigarh Housing Board — Flats and Allotment Services
schemes.department: Chandigarh Housing Board
schemes.brief: The Chandigarh Housing Board's own online counter — new scheme applications, instalment and rent payments, transfer of a flat, need-based change requests, no-dues certificates and the e-auction of leftover units. Almost everything an allottee used to queue for is here.
schemes.benefit: Board flat applications, payments, transfers and no-dues certificates online
eligibility: For a new scheme, the conditions set out in that scheme's brochure, usually including Chandigarh residence
For allottee services, you must be the recorded allottee or a legal heir
A transfer needs the dues cleared and the Board's permission before the deed
One flat per family under the subsidised categories
documents: Aadhaar card and PAN card
Allotment letter, for an existing allottee
Residence proof of Chandigarh
Income proof, for a category-based scheme
Latest payment receipts, for a no-dues certificate
Succession certificate or a will, for a transfer on inheritance
Passport-size photographs

demoFields.label: Service wanted
demoFields.hint: New scheme application, instalment or rent payment, transfer, need-based change, no-dues certificate, or e-auction. Pick the one you need.

demoFields.label: Allottee Name (as on the allotment letter)
demoFields.hint: As on the allotment letter, which is what the Board's record follows, even if Aadhaar spells it differently.

demoFields.label: Allotment / File Number
demoFields.hint: From the allotment letter. Every service is looked up against it, so keep the letter safe.

demoFields.label: Dwelling unit and sector
demoFields.hint: As recorded by the Board, which may differ from how the post office writes it.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar and PAN
demoFields.hint: Both are needed for a transfer or a new purchase, because it is a property transaction.

demoFields.label: Amount being paid (Rs.)
demoFields.hint: The portal shows what is due. Pay from that figure rather than an old demand letter, since interest may have been added.

demoFields.label: Reason, for a transfer or a change
demoFields.hint: For a transfer, say sale, gift or inheritance and attach the papers. A need-based change needs the sanctioned plan.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number and Email
demoFields.hint: The receipt, the demand notices and every Board notice come here.

demoSteps: Register on chbonline.in with your allotment or file number, Aadhaar and mobile, and confirm the OTP.
Choose the service. For a payment, check the amount the portal shows against your own record before paying — interest may have been added since the last demand.
Pay online and download the receipt at once. Keep every receipt until the final no-dues certificate is issued.
For a transfer, apply for the Board's permission first and clear the dues. A deed signed before that permission is not recognised.
For a new scheme, read the brochure for the price, the category and the closing date, then apply and pay the registration money in time.
Track the application on the portal by the file number, and take anything unresolved to the Board's office in Sector 9 with the application number.
schemes.helpline: 0172-4601826 — Chandigarh Housing Board

schemes.title: Chandigarh e-Services — Certificates and Citizen Services
schemes.department: Chandigarh Administration
schemes.brief: Chandigarh's single window for certificates and citizen services — residence, income, caste, birth and death registration, and a range of departmental permissions. The e-Sampark centres across the sectors do the same things across a counter.
schemes.benefit: Residence, income, caste and birth certificates applied for online or at an e-Sampark centre
eligibility: Resident of Chandigarh, applying from the address where you live
A residence certificate needs proof that you have lived in Chandigarh for the qualifying period
A caste certificate needs the caste to be on the Chandigarh SC or OBC list
An income certificate is valid for one year
documents: Aadhaar card of the applicant
Ration card or voter card as residence proof
Electricity or water bill for the address
Father's caste certificate or a school record, for a caste certificate
Salary slips or Form 16, for an income certificate
Passport-size photograph and a scanned signature

demoFields.label: Service wanted
demoFields.hint: Residence, income, caste, birth or death certificate, or a departmental permission. Each has its own form and fee.

demoFields.label: Applicant Name (as on Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: Letter for letter as on Aadhaar. The certificate prints from this entry.

demoFields.label: Father's / Husband's Name
demoFields.hint: Used to identify the family in the records; essential for a caste certificate.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number
demoFields.hint: Twelve digits. Identity is confirmed on this and the OTP goes to the linked mobile.

demoFields.label: Full address with sector and house number
demoFields.hint: The address you actually live at. The verification is done there.

demoFields.label: Years resident in Chandigarh
demoFields.hint: For a residence certificate, say from when. The ration card, school records or an old electricity bill are what prove it.

demoFields.label: Annual Family Income (Rs.)
demoFields.hint: For an income certificate, the household's total for the year. Keep it consistent with the salary slips you upload.

demoFields.label: Purpose
demoFields.value: College admission under the Chandigarh quota
demoFields.hint: Written for the record. It does not restrict where the certificate is used.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: The application number and the ready message come here by SMS.

demoSteps: Register on eservices.chd.gov.in with your mobile, or walk into any e-Sampark centre, which files it across the counter for the notified fee.
Choose the certificate and fill the form from your Aadhaar and the address proof.
Upload the documents, pay the fee online, and keep the application number from the acknowledgement.
The area official verifies the address, usually within a week. Be reachable on the mobile you gave.
The signed certificate is issued and downloaded from the same login, or collected at the e-Sampark centre.
If it runs past the time the service promises, quote the application number to the Deputy Commissioner's office.
schemes.helpline: 0172-2703172 — e-Sampark, Chandigarh Administration

schemes.title: Krishak Unnati Yojana (Paddy Difference Amount)
schemes.department: Agriculture Development & Farmers Welfare Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, with the Food Department and cooperative societies (paddy procurement)
schemes.brief: Chhattisgarh pays its farmers Rs 3,100 a quintal for paddy. The cooperative society pays the central MSP when you sell, and Krishak Unnati Yojana later pays the gap between MSP and Rs 3,100, on up to 21 quintals an acre, straight into your bank account. You do not fill a separate form for it. You only need to be registered at your cooperative society for paddy sale and sell your paddy there in the procurement season. Farmers who sold paddy earlier and now sow pulses, oilseeds or maize instead also get per-acre help under the same scheme.
schemes.benefit: Gap between MSP and Rs 3,100 a quintal on up to 21 quintals an acre: Rs 731 a quintal (Rs 15,351 an acre) for common paddy in kharif 2025-26
eligibility: A farmer in Chhattisgarh registered for paddy sale at a primary cooperative society (sewa sahkari samiti or LAMPS)
From the 2026-27 season the AgriStack Farmer ID is the registration; the society enters your land, bank and nominee details. The last date given for 2026-27 was 31 October 2026
You must actually sell your paddy at the society's procurement centre in the season (mid-November to January). The limit is 21 quintals an acre, on the area shown in the Digital Crop Survey
Sharecroppers (adhiya, rega), forest rights patta holders, village kotwars and registered institutions can also register; they were exempted from AgriStack in 2025-26
Farmers who sold paddy at MSP the previous year and now grow pulses, oilseeds or maize instead get input help per acre after the crop area is checked
documents: Aadhaar card, with the mobile number linked to it
AgriStack Farmer ID (Kisan ID)
B-1 and khasra (P-II) copy of your land, and the Kisan Kitab (Rin Pustika)
Bank passbook of an account in the farmer's own name, linked to Aadhaar
Name and Aadhaar of a nominee
Sharecroppers: the written adhiya or rega agreement with the land owner; forest land: the van adhikar patra
schemes.submitAt: Go to the primary cooperative society (sewa sahkari samiti or LAMPS) where your village sells paddy, before the registration deadline (31 October for the 2026-27 season). Take your Aadhaar card, AgriStack Farmer ID, B-1 and khasra copy, Kisan Kitab and bank passbook. If you do not have a Farmer ID yet, the society operator can make it for you on the spot, or you can make it at a CSC or yourself on cgfr.agristack.gov.in. Farmers who sold at the society last year are already on its list and only need to check that their land and bank details are correct.

demoFields.label: Name of farmer
demoFields.hint: Your name exactly as on the land record (B-1) and Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Father's / husband's name
demoFields.hint: As written in the land record.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own Aadhaar. The OTP goes to the mobile linked to it.

demoFields.label: AgriStack Farmer ID
demoFields.hint: The Kisan ID from the farmer registry. The society cannot register you for 2026-27 without it.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Token messages and payment messages come to this number.

demoFields.label: Village and society
demoFields.hint: The society where your village's paddy is bought.

demoFields.label: Khasra numbers and area
demoFields.hint: Copy from the B-1. Only this area, as seen in the crop survey, counts for the 21 quintal an acre limit.

demoFields.label: Area sown with paddy
demoFields.hint: The area actually under paddy this season. If you sowed pulses or maize instead, tell the society; it counts for crop-change help.

demoFields.label: Bank account and IFSC
demoFields.hint: Usually the district cooperative bank account linked to the society. MSP and the Krishak Unnati amount both come here.

demoFields.label: Nominee
demoFields.hint: The person who can receive the money if something happens to you.

demoSteps: Make your AgriStack Farmer ID if you do not have one, at the society, a CSC or on cgfr.agristack.gov.in, using your Aadhaar and land details.
Before 31 October, go to your cooperative society and get your land, bank and nominee details entered for the paddy season.
When procurement opens in mid-November, take a token for your selling day from the society or on the Token Tuhar Hath app.
Bring your paddy to the procurement centre on the token date. It is weighed and bought at MSP, and the MSP amount reaches your bank account within a few days.

After the season, the state pays the Krishak Unnati difference (Rs 3,100 minus MSP, for every quintal you sold) into the same account in one go. The 2025-26 amount was paid in early 2026, before Holi.
If the money does not come, take your sale receipt and passbook to the society manager or the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer (RAEO) and ask them to check your entry.
schemes.helpline: 1800-180-1551 (Kisan Call Centre). For registration or payment problems, ask the society manager, the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer (RAEO) or your tehsil office

schemes.title: Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Ayushman Swasthya Yojana (Ayushman Card)
schemes.department: State Nodal Agency, Directorate of Health Services, Health & Family Welfare Department, Government of Chhattisgarh, with the National Health Authority
schemes.brief: Chhattisgarh's free hospital treatment scheme for every family with a ration card. It used to be called the Dr. Khubchand Baghel Swasthya Sahayata Yojana and was renamed in 2024. Antyodaya and Priority (BPL) ration card families get cashless treatment up to Rs 5 lakh a year with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, and other (APL) ration card families get up to Rs 50,000 a year, at empanelled government and private hospitals. You show the Ayushman card at the hospital. You can make it on the Ayushman portal or app, or free at the hospital's Ayushman desk with your Aadhaar and ration card.
schemes.benefit: Rs 5 lakh a year for BPL families, Rs 50,000 a year for APL families, cashless
eligibility: Families with an Antyodaya or Priority (BPL) ration card from the Chhattisgarh Food Department: up to Rs 5 lakh a year
Families with any other (APL) Chhattisgarh ration card: up to Rs 50,000 a year
Every person aged 70 and above, whatever the income, can also get Rs 5 lakh under the Ayushman Vay Vandana card
Covers about 1,961 treatments, including cancer, heart and kidney care, dialysis, joint replacement, cataract and newborn care
Tests up to 7 days before admission, and check-ups and medicines up to 10 days after discharge, are included
For very costly rare illnesses beyond this cover, BPL families can ask for help of up to Rs 25 lakh under the separate Mukhyamantri Vishesh Swasthya Sahayata Yojana
documents: Aadhaar card of each family member, for e-KYC
Family ration card
Mobile number for the OTP
A live photo, taken on the phone or at the hospital desk during e-KYC
At admission: the Ayushman card, with the ration card and Aadhaar card

demoFields.label: Login as
demoFields.hint: Choose Beneficiary when you are making the card for yourself or your family.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Any number you keep with you. The login OTP and the approval message come here.

demoFields.label: Scheme and state
demoFields.hint: Choose the state Chhattisgarh. The state scheme cards are made on the same Ayushman system.

demoFields.label: Search your family by
demoFields.hint: The ration card number brings up the whole family at once. If nothing comes, search with your Aadhaar number.

demoFields.label: Ration card number
demoFields.hint: Copy it from your ration card. If your family is not found, go to the Ayushman desk of any empanelled hospital with the ration card and Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number for e-KYC
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar of the member whose card you are making now. Each member is done one at a time.

demoFields.label: e-KYC method
demoFields.hint: Use Aadhaar OTP if the mobile is linked to Aadhaar, otherwise choose face authentication.

demoFields.label: Live photo
demoFields.hint: Face straight, good light, no cap or dark glasses. A blurred photo gets the request rejected.

demoFields.label: Relation with head of family
demoFields.hint: How this member is related to the person named first on the ration card.

demoFields.label: District and PIN code
demoFields.hint: Where you live now, so nearby empanelled hospitals are shown.

demoSteps: Open beneficiary.nha.gov.in or the Ayushman app and log in as Beneficiary with your mobile number and OTP.
Choose Chhattisgarh and search for your family by ration card number or Aadhaar.
Next to each member whose e-KYC is pending, verify with Aadhaar OTP or face authentication and take the live photo.
Submit. The state agency checks the request, usually within a day or two, and you get an SMS.
Log in again and download the Ayushman card. If you cannot do it on the phone, the Ayushman desk at any empanelled hospital, a CSC or a choice centre makes it free.
At the hospital, go to the Ayushman Mitra desk with the card, ration card and Aadhaar. Do not pay cash for a treatment covered by the scheme; call 104 if anyone asks for money.
schemes.helpline: 104 (Ayushman Chhattisgarh helpline) / 14555 (Ayushman Bharat national helpline)

schemes.title: Chhattisgarh e-District — Income, Caste and Residence Certificates
schemes.department: Chhattisgarh Infotech Promotion Society (CHiPS), Government of Chhattisgarh
schemes.brief: Chhattisgarh e-District issues the certificates a citizen is asked for again and again — income, caste, domicile or residence, birth, death and marriage — along with other revenue, social welfare and licensing services. You apply, upload the documents, pay the fee, track the file by its reference number and download the signed certificate as a PDF. The citizen login sits at cgedistrict.cgstate.gov.in, and newer services are being moved to the state's Sewa Setu platform at sewasetu.cgstate.gov.in.
schemes.benefit: Income, caste, domicile and civil registration certificates applied for online and downloaded as a signed PDF
eligibility: Resident of Chhattisgarh, applying in the district and tehsil where you live

Caste certificate: your community must appear in Chhattisgarh's own notified SC, ST or OBC list, and the claim is traced through your father's record — a certificate from another state is not accepted here
Domicile or residence certificate: the family must have lived in Chhattisgarh continuously, normally shown by a land record, school record or old voter entry
Income certificate: the figure is the whole family's income for the financial year from all sources, and a patwari enquiry may be held on it
Birth, death and marriage certificates are applied for by the person concerned or an immediate family member
A working mobile number, since registration and every status message run on OTP
documents: Aadhaar card of the applicant
Ration card of the family
Proof of address — voter ID, electricity bill or the panchayat/ward certificate
Father's caste certificate or an old school record showing the caste, for a caste certificate
Land record (B-1 / khasra-khatauni) or an old school transfer certificate, for domicile
Income proof — salary slip, Form 16, or the patwari's or sarpanch's income statement
Self-declaration or affidavit on the form the service page gives
Recent passport-size photograph, scanned

demoFields.label: Select Service
demoFields.hint: Pick the service before anything else. Each one has its own document list and its own fee, shown on the service page.

demoFields.label: Applicant Name (Hindi and English)
demoFields.value: रमेश कुमार साहू / Ramesh Kumar Sahu
demoFields.hint: Both boxes must carry the same name. The certificate prints from the Hindi box, so check the spelling there carefully.

demoFields.label: Father's / Husband's Name
demoFields.hint: As on Aadhaar. For a caste certificate the officer traces the claim through the father, so this must match the record you upload.

demoFields.label: Date of Birth
demoFields.hint: From the school certificate or birth certificate you are uploading.

demoFields.label: Gender
demoFields.hint: As on Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number
demoFields.hint: The 12 digits on your own Aadhaar. The portal matches the name and date of birth against it.

demoFields.label: District / Tehsil / Village or Ward
demoFields.hint: The file goes to the tehsildar of the tehsil named here. Give the place you actually live, not a relative's address.

demoFields.label: Annual Family Income (Rs.)
demoFields.hint: The whole family's income for the financial year from every source. The patwari may verify it, and a figure that does not match what he reports gets the application rejected.

demoFields.label: Purpose of the Certificate
demoFields.hint: Write what you need it for. Scholarships, admissions and scheme applications each want the certificate issued recently, so apply close to the time you need it.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number and Email
demoFields.hint: The reference number and every status update come here. Keep the number active until the certificate is downloaded.

demoSteps: Open edistrict.cgstate.gov.in, go to the citizen login and register once with your mobile number and the OTP.
Choose the service, read its document list, fill the form in Hindi and English where both are asked, and upload the scans.
Pay the fee online if the service charges one, submit, and note the reference number the screen shows.
The file reaches the patwari and then the tehsildar or the concerned officer. A field enquiry is normal for income, caste and domicile certificates, so keep the original documents ready at home.
Track the file by the reference number on the portal. It names the officer holding it and the stage it has reached.
Download the approved certificate as a PDF from the same login and print it. The digital signature on it makes it valid without any further stamp.
If it is rejected, the reason is written on the portal. Fix that one point and apply again, or take the reference number to the Lok Seva Kendra or the Collectorate.
schemes.helpline: No public helpline number is published for the portal. Ask at the Lok Seva Kendra or Choice Centre in your tehsil, or at the e-District cell in your District Collectorate.

schemes.title: Mahtari Vandan Yojana — Monthly Assistance for Married Women
schemes.department: Women and Child Development Department, Government of Chhattisgarh
schemes.brief: Mahtari Vandan Yojana pays Rs 1,000 a month — Rs 12,000 in a year — to an eligible married woman of Chhattisgarh, straight into her own bank account. Widowed, divorced and abandoned women are covered along with married women. Fresh registration opens only in windows announced by the department; between those windows the portal is still used to check the application status, read the provisional and final beneficiary lists, file an objection and follow each instalment.
schemes.benefit: Rs 1,000 a month, Rs 12,000 a year, into the woman's own Aadhaar-seeded account
eligibility: Married woman who is a permanent resident of Chhattisgarh; widowed, divorced and abandoned women are also eligible
Must have completed 21 years of age on 1 January of the year the registration window opens

The family must have no income-tax payer, and no member in a regular or contractual post of the central or state government, a board, corporation or government undertaking — class IV and group D posts are not counted
No one in the family may be a sitting or former MP or MLA, or the chairman or vice-chairman of a board or corporation
A woman already drawing a government social pension gets only the difference, up to Rs 1,000 a month
A bank account in the woman's own name, seeded with Aadhaar and DBT-enabled; a husband's or joint account will not receive the money
documents: Aadhaar card of the woman and of her husband
Bank passbook first page in the woman's own name, Aadhaar-seeded and DBT-enabled
Residence proof of Chhattisgarh — ration card, voter ID or domicile certificate
Age proof — school certificate, birth certificate or the Aadhaar date of birth
Marriage certificate, or the self-declaration the portal provides where there is none
Death certificate of the husband for a widow, or the court order for a divorced woman
Recent passport-size photograph
The signed self-declaration and undertaking form printed from the portal

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Number of the applicant
demoFields.hint: The application starts from the woman's own Aadhaar and an OTP to the mobile number linked to it. If no mobile is linked to your Aadhaar, get that done at an Aadhaar centre first — nothing else can be filled until then.

demoFields.label: Applicant Name
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on Aadhaar and on the bank passbook. A difference between the two is the single most common reason the money does not arrive.

demoFields.label: Husband's Name
demoFields.hint: As on his Aadhaar. For a widow, write the husband's name as on his death certificate.

demoFields.label: Date of Birth
demoFields.hint: From Aadhaar. You must have completed 21 years on 1 January of the year the window opened, so check this date against that.

demoFields.label: Marital Status
demoFields.hint: Married, widow, divorced or abandoned. Choosing widow or divorced means you must upload the death certificate or the court order.

demoFields.label: Category
demoFields.hint: General, SC, ST or OBC. The amount is the same for everyone; this is only recorded.

demoFields.label: District / Block / Village or Ward
demoFields.hint: The place you live. Your form is verified by the Anganwadi worker and the supervisor of this area, so a wrong address stalls the check.

demoFields.label: Anganwadi Centre or Ward Office
demoFields.hint: The centre that serves your locality. The Anganwadi worker can fill and submit the form for you if you cannot do it yourself.

demoFields.label: Bank Account Number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: The woman's own account, Aadhaar-seeded and DBT-enabled. Ask the bank to confirm the DBT seeding — an ordinary account with the Aadhaar number merely written in the file is not enough.

demoFields.label: Mobile Number
demoFields.hint: The OTP, the application number and each monthly payment message come here.

demoSteps: Check that registration is open. The portal announces the window; outside it you can still see the lists and the payment status but cannot submit a new form.
Get the bank account right before you apply — in the woman's own name, Aadhaar-seeded and DBT-enabled. The bank does this free of charge.
Open mahtarivandan.cgstate.gov.in and start the application with the woman's Aadhaar number and the OTP, or ask the Anganwadi worker, the ward office or the gram panchayat to fill it for you.
Fill the form, upload the documents and submit. Note the application number and take a printout of the acknowledgement.

The Anganwadi worker and the supervisor verify the details. Your name then appears in the provisional beneficiary list published on the portal — check it, and if a name is wrongly included or wrongly left out, file an objection on the portal within the days allowed.
After the objections are settled, the final list is published. Confirm your name is in it.

Rs 1,000 reaches the account every month by direct transfer. The portal's payment status page shows each instalment; if one is missing, check the bank for a seeding failure first, then take the application number to the Anganwadi centre or the District Programme Officer, Women and Child Development.
schemes.helpline: No toll-free number is published on the portal. Ask your Anganwadi worker, the ward office or gram panchayat, or the District Programme Officer, Women and Child Development, in your district.

schemes.title: Pension Scheme to Old Age Persons (Senior Citizen) — DNH and Daman & Diu

schemes.title: DDA Housing Schemes and e-Auction
schemes.department: Delhi Development Authority
schemes.brief: The Delhi Development Authority sells flats through its own e-Services portal — some on first come first served, some by draw of lots and some by e-auction. Recent rounds have included the Sasta Ghar and Madhyam Vargiya schemes, Dwarka flats, the Janta, Jan Sadharan, Sabka Ghar and Shramik Awaas Yojana of 2025, and the Nagrik, Karmajeevi and Towering Heights schemes of 2026. You register with PAN and a mobile OTP, pay the registration money online and book or bid from the same login. On a first come first served scheme the flat you pick must be paid for within 30 minutes, so the money has to be ready before you start.

demoSteps: Open eservices.dda.org.in, see which schemes are live and download the brochure. The price, the category, the area and the payment schedule are all in it.
Register with your PAN, mobile number and email, confirm the OTP, and pay the registration fee online.
Fill the application for the scheme and category you qualify for, upload the documents, and pay the registration money from your own account.

On a first come first served scheme, pick the flat from the live inventory and pay within 30 minutes of selection or the flat goes back into the pool — arrange the funds and the transfer limit beforehand. On a draw-of-lots scheme, wait for the result on the portal. On an e-auction, bid within the auction window.
If you are not allotted a flat, the registration money is refunded to the account you gave. Keep the acknowledgement until it arrives.
On allotment, download the demand-cum-allotment letter and pay the instalments by the dates written in it. Missing a date attracts interest and eventually cancellation.

After full payment the conveyance deed is executed and possession is given. Inspect the flat, get every defect recorded in writing before taking the keys, and keep the allotment letter and the deed together.
schemes.helpline: No toll-free number is published on the e-Services portal. Take the registration number to the Housing Branch of the Delhi Development Authority at Vikas Sadan, INA, New Delhi, or use the grievance link on dda.gov.in.

schemes.department: Department of Women and Child Development, Govt of NCT of Delhi
schemes.brief: Rs 2,500 a month for women aged 21 to 60 from low-income Delhi families. It was announced as the Mahila Samriddhi Yojana and renamed the Delhi Lakshmi Yojana when it started on 1 August 2026. You choose how the money comes: Rs 1,000 a month into a digital rupee (CBDC) wallet to spend and Rs 1,500 into a locked deposit, or the full Rs 2,500 into the deposit. The deposit stays locked till 31 July 2029, and you apply online on the scheme's own portal.

You, your husband or one of your parents must have lived in Delhi for at least 10 years
Not for income-tax payers, GST filers, women already getting any government pension, or families where anyone is a government employee (regular or contract) or owns a four-wheeler
Family electricity use of 2,400 units a year or less, not more than three living children, and no criminal record

The pregnancy is registered with the ASHA or ANM at the first antenatal check-up
The delivery must take place in a government or private hospital, not at home
documents: Woman's Aadhaar card
Bank or post office account in her own name, linked with Aadhaar
Mamta card (mother and child card) from the health centre
Proof of group: caste certificate, NFSA or BPL ration card, PMJAY card, e-Shram card, MGNREGA job card or disability certificate - or an income certificate up to Rs.8 lakh
Mobile number
Hospital delivery certificate or discharge paper (for the delivery instalment)
Baby's birth certificate and the vaccination entries on the Mamta card (for the last instalment)
schemes.submitAt: At your first antenatal check-up, ask your ASHA worker, or the ANM at the Anganwadi, sub-centre, Primary Health Centre (PHC) or Urban Health Centre, to register you under Namo Shri. Take your Aadhaar card, bank passbook, Mamta card and the proof of your group (or an income certificate). For the later instalments, show the same ANM the hospital delivery paper and the Mamta card with the baby's vaccine entries.

demoFields.label: Woman's name
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on her Aadhaar card. The bank account must be in the same name.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The pregnant woman's own Aadhaar, not her husband's.

demoFields.label: Husband's name
demoFields.hint: As on his Aadhaar or the ration card.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: A number she or the family keeps. Messages about each instalment come here.

demoFields.label: Date of last period (LMP)
demoFields.hint: First day of the last monthly period. The ANM uses it to work out the due date and the 6-month instalment.

demoFields.label: Mamta card / registration number
demoFields.hint: The number on the Mamta card given at the health centre. Keep the card safe - every check-up and vaccine is written on it.

demoFields.label: Group (category)
demoFields.hint: Pick the one group you can prove - SC, ST, NFSA or BPL card, PMJAY card, e-Shram, MGNREGA, farmer or disability - or give the income certificate.

demoFields.label: Number of live children
demoFields.hint: The help is only for the first two live children, so give the true number.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: Account in the woman's own name, seeded with Aadhaar. A closed or dormant account is the main reason money does not arrive.

demoFields.label: Village / health centre
demoFields.hint: Where she lives now and the centre she goes to for check-ups.

demoSteps: As soon as you know you are pregnant, meet your ASHA worker or go to the nearest PHC or Urban Health Centre for the first check-up. You get a Mamta card there.
Ask the ANM to register you under Namo Shri. Give Aadhaar, passbook, Mamta card and your group proof or income certificate, and check that your bank details are typed correctly.
The first instalment of Rs.5,000 comes to your account after registration (part central PM Matru Vandana money, part state).
After six months of pregnancy and the check-ups, Rs.2,000 more comes.
Deliver in a hospital - the 108 ambulance is free. After a hospital delivery Rs.3,000 comes.
Register the baby's birth and get the vaccines up to 14 weeks written on the Mamta card. The last Rs.2,000 then comes.
If an instalment does not arrive, ask the ANM to check the status first. Most delays are a bank account not linked with Aadhaar.
schemes.helpline: Your ASHA worker or the ANM at the health centre; Gujarat health helpline 104

schemes.title: iKhedut Farm Subsidy - Equipment & Inputs
schemes.department: Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation Department, Gujarat
schemes.brief: Subsidy on farm equipment and inputs - rotavator, pump set, thresher, sprayer, drip irrigation, seeds and plant protection items. Applications open only in windows the department announces, so the portal is closed most of the year. The whole site is in Gujarati. Very few farmers apply from home: most go to the Village Computer Entrepreneur (VCE) at the e-Gram centre in the Gram Panchayat, who fills the form and prints it.
schemes.benefit: 25% to 75% of the cost, with a ceiling fixed for each item
eligibility: Farmer with agricultural land in Gujarat, held in the applicant's own name
7/12 and 8-A land records must show the applicant's name
Higher rates of subsidy for small and marginal farmers, women farmers and SC/ST farmers
One item can be claimed again only after the cycle fixed for it (a tractor, for example, only once in several years)
One application per item per window; the same family cannot claim the same item twice
documents: 7/12 and 8-A extracts of the land (download free from AnyRoR)
Aadhaar card
First page of the bank passbook or a cancelled cheque
Caste certificate, if claiming the SC or ST rate
Ration card
Quotation from a dealer approved by the department, where the item needs one

demoFields.label: Farmer's name (as on the 7/12)
demoFields.hint: Write the name exactly as it is printed on the land record, not a short form.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Your own 12-digit Aadhaar number. It must be the one linked to your bank account, or the subsidy will not reach you.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: A number you actually carry. Every message about approval and inspection comes to it.

demoFields.label: District / Taluka / Village
demoFields.hint: Pick from the drop-downs. Choose the village where the land is, not where you live, if the two are different.

demoFields.label: Survey number (from 7/12)
demoFields.hint: Copy it letter for letter from the 7/12, including 'paiki' and the part number.

demoFields.label: Khata number (from 8-A)
demoFields.hint: The account number on the 8-A extract. It covers all your survey numbers in that village.

demoFields.label: Component applied for
demoFields.hint: Choose the exact item and size. If you buy a different size later, the subsidy is refused.

demoFields.label: Land area for this item (hectare)
demoFields.hint: Area as shown on the 7/12, in hectares. One vigha is roughly 0.16 hectare.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: The account must be in the applicant's own name and Aadhaar-seeded. A joint account in the father's name is a common reason for failed payment.

demoFields.label: Category
demoFields.hint: General, SC, ST or OBC. Say SC or ST only if you can attach the certificate.

demoSteps: Check on the portal whether the window for your scheme group is open - Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry or Fisheries each open separately.
Choose 'Apply as an individual farmer'. If you have applied before, say yes and give your registration number instead of registering again.
Fill the form. The portal is in Gujarati; type names in Gujarati as they appear on the land record.
Save the form and note the application number that appears.
Now confirm the application. This is the step people miss - an application that is saved but not confirmed is treated as never made, and it cannot be confirmed after the window shuts.
Print the confirmed application and sign it.

Attach the 7/12, 8-A, Aadhaar, bank passbook copy and caste certificate, and hand the set to the Gram Sevak, the Taluka Agriculture Office or the VCE at the e-Gram centre within the days printed on the form.
Wait for pre-approval (purva manjuri). Do not buy the item before it comes - a purchase made earlier gets no subsidy.
Buy from an approved dealer, submit the bill and the dealer's certificate.
An officer inspects the item, and the subsidy is credited to your bank account by DBT.
schemes.helpline: Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551, or your Taluka Agriculture Officer / Gram Sevak

schemes.title: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swavalamban Yojana (MYSY)
schemes.department: Knowledge Consortium of Gujarat, Education Department
schemes.brief: Fee, hostel and book help for students of middle-income families who did well in the board exam. It is meant for the student who got the marks but whose family cannot pay the college fee. The portal works in Gujarati and English. After filling the form online you still have to carry the printout and your original certificates to an MYSY help centre - the application is not complete until that verification is done.
schemes.benefit: Tuition help up to Rs.2 lakh a year for medical and dental, Rs.50,000 a year for degree and diploma courses, plus Rs.12,000 hostel help and a book grant
eligibility: 80th percentile or above in the Class 10 board exam for a diploma, or Class 12 for a degree course
Family income up to Rs.6 lakh a year
Studying in a recognised college or institute in Gujarat
Admission taken through the official admission committee, or against a management seat where the scheme allows it
Renewal every year needs a pass result and the attendance the college certifies
documents: Class 10 and Class 12 marksheets
Income certificate from the Mamlatdar, issued within the period the portal states
Fee receipt and the admission letter
Aadhaar card
Bank passbook in the student's own name
Proof that the family home is far from the college, for the hostel grant
Self-declaration on the form the portal provides

demoFields.label: Student's name
demoFields.hint: Exactly as printed on the Class 10 marksheet. The board record is what the portal checks against.

demoFields.label: Class 12 seat number and year
demoFields.hint: From your board marksheet. The portal pulls your percentile from this, so one wrong digit stops the form.

demoFields.label: Percentile
demoFields.hint: The percentile printed on the marksheet, not the percentage. 80 and above qualifies.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The student's own Aadhaar, seeded to the student's own bank account.

demoFields.label: Course and college
demoFields.value: B.E. Civil, first year, government engineering college, Rajkot
demoFields.hint: Course, year of study and the full name of the institute as it appears on the admission letter.

demoFields.label: Family annual income
demoFields.hint: The figure on the Mamlatdar's income certificate, counting both parents. It must be Rs.6 lakh or less.

demoFields.label: Income certificate number and date
demoFields.hint: From the certificate issued by the Mamlatdar or the Jan Seva Kendra. An old certificate is rejected.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: The student's own savings account. A parent's account is not accepted.

demoFields.label: Hostel help needed
demoFields.value: Yes - home at Limbasi, Kheda; college at Rajkot
demoFields.hint: Say yes only if you stay in a hostel or on rent because the college is far. Keep the rent agreement or hostel receipt ready.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: The user id and PIN for the portal come to this number by SMS. Use the student's own number.

demoSteps: Get the income certificate first, from the Mamlatdar's office or a Jan Seva Kendra. It takes a few days and the form cannot be completed without it.
Register on the MYSY portal with the student's mobile number. A user id and PIN come back by SMS - write them down, you need them every year for renewal.
Log in and choose the right form: fresh application if this is the first year, renewal if you got the help last year.
Fill the form. Switch the portal to Gujarati if that is easier to read; the entries are the same either way.
Upload the marksheets, income certificate, fee receipt and bank passbook as clear scans.
Submit and print the application.
Take the printout with all original certificates to the nearest MYSY help centre. These sit inside selected colleges and the portal lists them district by district.
The officer at the help centre checks the originals and gives an acknowledgement. Keep it - it is your proof of applying.
Track the status on the portal with your user id.
The amount comes to the student's bank account by DBT, usually in parts as the college confirms the fee.
Apply again the next year with the new marksheet. Missing a year's renewal ends the help.
schemes.helpline: MYSY help centre at your college - the portal lists one for every district

schemes.title: Post-Matric Scholarship for SC, ST, OBC and EBC Students
schemes.department: Scheduled Caste Welfare, Developing Castes Welfare and Tribal Development Departments, Gujarat
schemes.brief: Fee reimbursement and a maintenance allowance for students of SC, ST, OBC and EBC families studying after Class 10. Every one of these scholarships is applied for on Digital Gujarat with a single citizen account, and the site works in Gujarati, Hindi and English. Students without a computer at home usually do it at the college scholarship desk or at a Jan Seva Kendra.
schemes.benefit: Tuition and other compulsory fees reimbursed, plus a monthly maintenance allowance that is higher for hostellers
eligibility: Domicile of Gujarat, with a caste certificate for SC, ST, OBC or an EBC certificate
Studying a recognised course after Class 10, in Gujarat
Family income within the ceiling fixed for your category - it differs for SC, ST, OBC and EBC, and the current figure is shown on the portal before you apply
Not repeating the same year of the same course
One scholarship only - you cannot draw two government scholarships for the same year
documents: Caste certificate issued by the competent authority
Income certificate from the Mamlatdar or the Jan Seva Kendra
Last year's marksheet and the current admission or fee receipt
Aadhaar card
Bank passbook in the student's own name, Aadhaar-seeded
Hostel certificate from the warden, if claiming the hosteller rate
School leaving certificate

demoFields.label: Student's name
demoFields.hint: As on the Class 10 marksheet. The name must match the bank account too, or the transfer fails.

demoFields.label: Digital Gujarat registered mobile
demoFields.hint: One account, one mobile number. Use the student's own - the OTP for every login comes here.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: The student's Aadhaar. Check on the portal that it is seeded to the bank account before you submit.

demoFields.label: Caste and caste certificate number
demoFields.hint: Choose the category that matches your certificate. Applying under the wrong department's scheme is the commonest reason for rejection.

demoFields.label: Income certificate number and date
demoFields.hint: Must be within the validity the portal states, usually issued in the same financial year.

demoFields.label: Course, year and college
demoFields.value: B.Com, second year, arts and commerce college, Nadiad
demoFields.hint: Write the course exactly as the college registers it. The college has to approve your form online afterwards.

demoFields.label: Hosteller or day scholar
demoFields.hint: Say hosteller only with a warden's certificate. The maintenance rate is different for the two.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: The student's own account. Accounts in a parent's name, and dormant accounts, are rejected.

demoFields.label: Last year's marksheet and percentage
demoFields.hint: Upload the marksheet of the year just passed. A student who failed and is repeating the year cannot claim again.

demoSteps: Create one Digital Gujarat citizen account with your mobile number and an OTP. Do not make a second account later - all your years of scholarship sit under this one.
Switch the site to Gujarati from the language button at the top if that is easier to read.
Complete your profile first, including Aadhaar and bank details. The scholarship form pulls from it.
Open 'Scholarship' services and pick the scheme that matches your certificate - Scheduled Caste, Tribal, Developing Castes (OBC) or EBC. Each is run by a different department.
Fill the form, upload the caste certificate, income certificate, marksheet, fee receipt and passbook.
Submit, and print the acknowledgement.
Hand the printout and originals to your college scholarship clerk. The college has to verify the application on its own login - until it does, nothing moves.
The district officer of the concerned department sanctions the amount.
The fee part goes to the college and the maintenance part comes to your account by DBT.
Apply again at the start of each academic year, as soon as the portal opens; the window closes well before the exams.
schemes.helpline: Digital Gujarat helpdesk 1800-233-5500, or your college scholarship desk

schemes.title: Manav Kalyan Yojana (Free Tool Kit by e-Voucher)
schemes.department: Commissioner of Cottage & Rural Industries, Industries & Mines Department, Gujarat
schemes.brief: A free tool kit for starting a small trade: beauty parlour, embroidery, plumbing, vehicle servicing and repair, papad making, pickle making, electric appliance repair, milk and curd selling, puncture repair or centring work. Since 2024 the kit comes as an e-voucher (a QR code) that you use at an approved dealer, and you can also choose 5 days of training paid at Rs.500 a day. The old Manav Garima Yojana has been merged into this scheme; tailoring, carpentry, cobbler, barber and some other trades moved to PM Vishwakarma. You apply on the e-Kutir portal when the yearly window opens (the 2026-27 window opened on 17 June 2026), and when there are more applicants than kits a computerised draw decides.
schemes.benefit: A free tool kit for one of 10 trades through an e-voucher, plus optional training at Rs.500 a day
eligibility: Age between 18 and 60
Family income up to Rs.6 lakh a year, in villages and cities alike; no income limit for the 12 most backward SC castes and the most backward, nomadic and denotified SEBC groups
One kit per family, only once
No member of the family should be a government employee
Must have an e-Shram card
Widows, BPL card holders (score 0 to 16) and the lowest incomes get priority, and 5% of kits are kept for disabled applicants
documents: Aadhaar card
e-Shram card
Caste certificate
Income certificate up to Rs.6 lakh from the Mamlatdar, TDO, Nagarpalika Chief Officer or Municipal Corporation officer (not needed for the groups with no income limit)
Proof of age - school leaving certificate or birth certificate
BPL card or ration card, if you have one
Husband's death certificate, for widows claiming priority
Bank passbook

demoFields.label: Full name (in English, as per Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on Aadhaar. The form can be switched to Gujarati from the language option.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar card number
demoFields.hint: Your own number. Forgot your user ID later? It can be found with Aadhaar and birth date.

demoFields.label: Gender
demoFields.hint: Pick as on Aadhaar.

demoFields.label: Date of birth
demoFields.hint: DD/MM/YYYY. You must be between 18 and 60.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Your user ID and password come here by SMS, and later the e-voucher and dealer OTPs.

demoFields.label: Password
demoFields.hint: Make your own and keep it. If the VCE fills the form for you, still keep the user ID and password yourself.

demoFields.label: Trade (tool kit) chosen
demoFields.hint: Asked in the Manav Kalyan form after login. Pick one of the 10 trades; it cannot be changed after submitting.

demoFields.label: e-Shram card number
demoFields.hint: Required. If you have no e-Shram card, the form gives a link to make one first.

demoFields.label: Caste and income certificate
demoFields.hint: Upload clear photos of the originals as PDF or JPEG. Income must be up to Rs.6 lakh unless your caste group has no limit.

demoFields.label: Want basic training?
demoFields.hint: Choose Yes for 5 days of training with Rs.500 a day for attendance. Choose No to get the e-voucher directly.

demoSteps: When the yearly window is open, go to e-kutir.gujarat.gov.in and register as a new individual with your name, Aadhaar, birth date and mobile. The village VCE can also fill it for you free of cost.

Log in, complete the profile, open Manav Kalyan Yojana, choose one trade, fill the form and upload Aadhaar, e-Shram card, caste and income certificates and age proof. Submit - until you submit, it stays only as a draft.
The District Industries Centre checks the application, and selection is made by an online draw before a district committee. Track it under Application Status.
If selected, an e-voucher (QR code) with the kit's value comes by SMS and in your login or the e-Kutir app, which also lists approved dealers.
Go to any approved dealer, show the QR code and give the OTP sent to your phone. Pick the tools you want within the limit; you pay only if you choose tools costing more.
A verification team will visit your home to see the kit and take a photo. Keep and use the tools - if they are sold or missing, the money is taken back.
Never share your e-voucher or OTP with anyone except the approved dealer at the time of buying.
schemes.helpline: Manav Kalyan help desk 99099 26280 / 99099 26180; your District Industries Centre (DIC)

schemes.title: OJAS - Gujarat Government Job Applications
schemes.department: Recruiting Boards of the Government of Gujarat
schemes.brief: The single site where Gujarat's recruiting boards advertise and take applications - panchayat service, subordinate services, police and Lok Rakshak, forest and many more. The advertisements themselves are published in Gujarati. The application is not counted until you confirm it and get a confirmation number, and the fee can be paid online or by printing a challan and paying it at a computerised post office.
schemes.benefit: One registration to apply for state and panchayat service vacancies
eligibility: Age, qualification and other conditions are as stated in each advertisement, not on the site generally
Knowledge of Gujarati is required for most posts
Age relaxation for SC, ST, OBC, women and ex-servicemen, as the advertisement says
The fee is usually waived for SC, ST, ex-servicemen and physically handicapped candidates
Apply separately for every advertisement - one registration does not apply you to everything
documents: Photograph and signature scanned to the size the advertisement states, in the stated file size
Class 10 and Class 12 marksheets and the degree or diploma certificate
School leaving certificate
Caste certificate, and a non-creamy-layer certificate for OBC candidates
EWS certificate, where claimed
Aadhaar card
Computer course certificate (CCC), where the post requires it

demoFields.label: Advertisement number
demoFields.hint: Copy it from the advertisement. Each post has its own number and its own application.

demoFields.label: Post applied for
demoFields.hint: Read the advertisement fully before choosing. You cannot change the post after confirming.

demoFields.label: Candidate's name
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on the Class 10 marksheet. A different spelling later can cost you the appointment.

demoFields.label: Date of birth
demoFields.hint: As on the Class 10 marksheet. Age is counted on the date the advertisement fixes, not on the day you apply.

demoFields.label: Category
demoFields.hint: Claim a category only with a valid certificate in the government's own format. The fee and the age relaxation follow from it.

demoFields.label: Qualification and percentage
demoFields.hint: The qualification the post asks for, with the university and the year of passing.

demoFields.label: Photograph and signature
demoFields.value: Photo 10 kb JPG, signature 8 kb JPG
demoFields.hint: Follow the size in the advertisement exactly. An oversized file will not upload and a blurred signature gets the form rejected at the exam hall.

demoFields.label: Mobile number and email
demoFields.hint: Use your own, and keep them for the whole recruitment - the call letter notice comes here.

demoFields.label: Confirmation number
demoFields.hint: This number is the only proof that you applied. Note it down and keep the printout.

demoFields.label: Fee payment
demoFields.hint: Pay online, or print the challan and pay it at a computerised post office before the last date. An unpaid application is not considered.

demoSteps: Open the advertisement on OJAS and read it end to end - age, qualification, fee and the last date. They are published in Gujarati.
Click Apply for that advertisement and fill the form. Fill it yourself where you can; if a cyber cafe or Jan Seva Kendra types it for you, sit with them and keep your own user id and password.
Upload the photograph and signature in the exact size stated.
Save the form, then confirm it. This is the step candidates lose their year on - an unconfirmed application is not an application, and it cannot be confirmed after the last date.
Note the confirmation number that appears.
Pay the fee online, or print the challan and pay it at a computerised post office within the days allowed.
Print the confirmed application and keep it with the fee receipt until the whole recruitment is over.
Download the call letter from the same site when it is released; it is not posted to you.
Carry the call letter and an original photo ID to the exam hall.
Check the site for the answer key, results and document verification notices - all of it is published here and nowhere else.
schemes.helpline: The helpdesk number printed on the advertisement you are applying against

schemes.title: e-Nirman Card - Construction Worker Registration (BOCW)
schemes.department: Gujarat Building & Other Construction Workers' Welfare Board, Labour, Skill Development & Employment Department
schemes.brief: The e-Nirman card registers a construction worker with the Gujarat construction workers' welfare board. With it you and your family can eat a full meal for Rs.5 at Shramik Annapurna centres, you are covered under the PMJAY-MA health card, and you can apply on the Sanman portal for the board's schemes - maternity help, children's education, housing help, illness and accident help. You can register yourself on the e-Nirman portal or app, or at a CSC, e-Gram centre, e-Shram Seva Kendra or Dhanvantari Arogya Rath. The card is valid for 3 years and is renewed with a fresh 90-day work certificate.
schemes.benefit: Rs.5 meals, Rs.7,500 maternity help for women workers, up to Rs.1.6 lakh extra housing help and more
eligibility: Age between 18 and 60
Did construction work for more than 90 days in the last 12 months (a self-declared or employer's certificate)
Does physical work on building or other construction - mason, labourer, carpenter, plumber, electrician, welder, tiles, painting, centring, road and MGNREGA work and the other listed jobs
No income limit for manual workers; office staff, supervisors and independent contractors cannot register
The card must be renewed every 3 years with a new 90-day work certificate to keep getting benefits
documents: Aadhaar card
Recent passport-size photo
Proof of age - birth certificate, school leaving certificate, voter ID or driving licence
Ration card or other proof of address
90-day work certificate from the employer or contractor, or a self-declaration
Bank passbook or cancelled cheque
Caste certificate, if you have one
Mobile number

demoFields.label: Full Name (as per Aadhaar)
demoFields.hint: Write it exactly as on the Aadhaar card, in English letters.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar Card Number
demoFields.hint: Your own 12-digit number. One Aadhaar can be registered only once.

demoFields.label: Gender
demoFields.hint: Women workers should register too - several schemes, such as maternity help, are only for them.

demoFields.label: Birthdate
demoFields.hint: As on Aadhaar, in DD/MM/YYYY. You must be between 18 and 60.

demoFields.label: Mobile No
demoFields.hint: Your user ID, password reset and approval messages come to this number.

demoFields.label: Email ID (not mandatory)
demoFields.hint: Leave it empty if you do not have one.

demoFields.label: Password
demoFields.hint: Make one you will remember and do not share it with the agent or contractor.

demoFields.label: User Type
demoFields.hint: Choose Construction Worker. Builders who pay the cess use a different login.

demoFields.label: Type of work and days worked
demoFields.value: Mason (kadiya) - 120 days in the last 12 months
demoFields.hint: Asked in the registration application after you log in. Upload the 90-day certificate signed by the contractor, or the self-declaration.

demoFields.label: Bank account number and IFSC
demoFields.hint: In your own name. The board pays all scheme money straight into this account.

demoSteps: Open the e-Nirman portal or the e-Nirman app and tap Register Yourself. Fill name, Aadhaar, gender, birth date, mobile, choose Construction Worker and set a password. Or get it done at a CSC, e-Gram centre, e-Shram Seva Kendra or the Dhanvantari Arogya Rath.
Log in and complete your profile - address, family members and bank account.
Open the application for Registration, fill your type of work and employer, and upload Aadhaar, photo, age proof, the 90-day work certificate and passbook. Submit and note the application number.
Check progress under View Citizen Application Status. The board's district office verifies the application.
When approved, download and print the e-Nirman card, or collect the print from the centre where you applied.
Show the card at any Shramik Annapurna centre for a Rs.5 meal, and apply for maternity, education, housing and other help on sanman.gujarat.gov.in.
Renew the card before 3 years are over with a new 90-day work certificate, or the benefits stop.
schemes.helpline: Gujarat BOCW Welfare Board toll-free 1800-233-2324; board office 079-25502271

schemes.title: PMJAY-MA Yojana - Mukhyamantri Amrutum (MA Card)
schemes.department: Health & Family Welfare Department, Gujarat (State Health Agency, PMJAY-MA)
schemes.brief: Gujarat's own health cover, joined with Ayushman Bharat: cashless treatment of up to Rs.10 lakh a year for the whole family at empanelled government and private hospitals. The old MA (Mukhyamantri Amrutum) and MA Vatsalya cards were merged into it in 2021 under the name PMJAY-MA, and in 2023 the cover was doubled from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.10 lakh. Gujarat covers many more families than the central list, including families earning up to Rs.4 lakh a year and senior citizens in families earning up to Rs.6 lakh. The card is the same Ayushman card, and you can make it yourself on the phone or at the kiosk of any government health centre or empanelled hospital.
schemes.benefit: Rs.10 lakh a year per family, cashless
eligibility: Families with an NFSA ration card or listed in the SECC-2011 list, and BPL families (rural BPL score 0 to 20, or urban UCD / Swarna Jayanti card)
Middle-class families with a yearly income of up to Rs.4 lakh, shown by an income certificate
Senior citizens aged 60 and above in families earning up to Rs.6 lakh a year; every person aged 70 and above gets the Vay Vandana card whatever the income
Registered construction workers (e-Nirman card), U-WIN card holders, ASHA and Anganwadi workers and helpers, accredited journalists and fixed-pay class 3 and 4 state employees
Gujarat government regular employees and pensioners, through their HRPN or PPO number
You must be a resident of Gujarat. There is no limit on family size, and illnesses you already have are covered
documents: Aadhaar card of each family member being enrolled (needed for e-KYC)
Ration card, for the family details
Income certificate from the Mamlatdar or TDO - for the Rs.4 lakh family category and for senior citizens up to Rs.6 lakh (it stays valid for 3 years)
BPL certificate, or your name in the approved BPL list, if you apply as a BPL family
Proof of your special category if any: e-Nirman card, U-WIN card, journalist accreditation, appointment letter, or HRPN / PPO number
Mobile number for the OTP

demoFields.label: Login as
demoFields.hint: Choose Beneficiary when you are making the card for yourself or your family. The Ayushman app on the phone works the same way.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Any working number you keep with you. The login OTP and the approval SMS come here.

demoFields.label: Scheme and state
demoFields.hint: Choose PMJAY and Gujarat. The PMJAY-MA card is made under the same scheme name.

demoFields.label: Search your family by
demoFields.hint: The ration card number usually brings up the whole family at once. You can also search by Aadhaar number.

demoFields.label: Ration card number
demoFields.hint: Copy it from your ration card. If no names come up, your family may need to be added at a kiosk - see the steps below.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number for e-KYC
demoFields.hint: Aadhaar of the member whose card you are making now. Each person is done one at a time.

demoFields.label: e-KYC method
demoFields.hint: Use the OTP if the mobile is linked to Aadhaar. If it is not, choose face authentication and scan the face on the phone camera.

demoFields.label: Live photo
demoFields.hint: Face straight, good light, no cap or dark glasses. A blurred photo gets the request sent back.

demoFields.label: Relation with head of family
demoFields.hint: How this member is related to the person named first on the ration card.

demoFields.label: District and PIN code
demoFields.hint: Where you live now, so the nearest empanelled hospitals are shown to you.

demoSteps: Open beneficiary.nha.gov.in or the Ayushman app, log in as Beneficiary with your mobile number and OTP, choose PMJAY and Gujarat, and search with your ration card number or Aadhaar.
If your family's names appear, tap e-KYC next to each member, verify with Aadhaar OTP or face scan, take the live photo and fill relation, district and PIN code. Then submit.

If your family does not appear but you qualify by income (up to Rs.4 lakh, or Rs.6 lakh for 60+) or as a construction worker or other listed group, go to the PMJAY-MA kiosk at the nearest government health centre (PHC, CHC, UHC, sub-district or district hospital) or at any empanelled hospital with your ration card, every member's Aadhaar and the income certificate or category proof.
The State Health Agency checks the request. Approval usually comes by SMS within a few days.
Log in again, open Download Card, verify with OTP and save the card for each family member on your phone, or take a printout.
Find an empanelled hospital on ma.gujarat.gov.in (Search - Empanelled Hospital). At the hospital, go to the PMJAY-MA or Ayushman Mitra desk with the card and Aadhaar.
Treatment for listed illnesses is cashless up to Rs.10 lakh a year for the family. Never pay cash for it - if a hospital asks, call 1800-233-1022.
schemes.helpline: PMJAY-MA toll-free 1800-233-1022 / Ayushman Bharat national helpline 14555

schemes.title: AnyRoR - 7/12 and 8-A Land Records
schemes.department: Revenue Department, Gujarat (e-Dhara)
schemes.brief: See and print the land record of any village in Gujarat - the 7/12 (village form 7 and 12) survey-wise, the 8-A khata-wise, and the mutation entries. Viewing is free and needs no login. The site and the extract are both in Gujarati. The copy you print here is unsigned and meant for information; for a bank loan or a court case take the digitally signed copy, or the stamped copy from the e-Dhara Kendra at your taluka Mamlatdar office.
schemes.benefit: Free view and print of 7/12, 8-A and entry records for any village in the state
eligibility: Open to anyone - no login is needed just to view a record
You need to know the district, taluka and village, and the survey number or khata number
The owner's name can be searched if you do not know the number
A registered login and a small fee are needed for a digitally signed copy
Urban property cards are under the separate urban section, not under 7/12
documents: Nothing is needed to view a record
Know your district, taluka and village
The survey number from an old 7/12, or the khata number from the 8-A
A mobile number, for the digitally signed copy

demoFields.label: Record wanted
demoFields.hint: VF-7 for the 7/12 by survey number, VF-8A for the khata, VF-6 for the mutation entries.

demoFields.label: Area type
demoFields.hint: Rural for village land. For a flat or plot inside a city, use the urban property card section instead.

demoFields.label: District
demoFields.hint: Choose from the list. If the district was split, pick the one the village falls under today.

demoFields.label: Taluka
demoFields.hint: The taluka the village belongs to. The village list changes once you pick this.

demoFields.label: Village
demoFields.hint: Pick from the drop-down. Village names repeat across talukas, so check the taluka first.

demoFields.label: Survey number
demoFields.hint: Exactly as on an old 7/12, with the 'paiki' part if there is one. A missing part number brings up the wrong plot.

demoFields.label: Khata number
demoFields.hint: Only for VF-8A. It lists every survey number the same owner holds in that village.

demoFields.label: Owner's name (to search)
demoFields.hint: Use this when you do not know the survey number. Type the name in Gujarati as it appears in the record.

demoFields.label: Verification code
demoFields.hint: Type the characters shown in the box. If it will not accept them, refresh for a new code.

demoSteps: Open the AnyRoR site and switch it to Gujarati if that is easier to read.
Choose 'View land record - rural' for village land, or the urban section for a city property.
Pick VF-7 for the 7/12, VF-8A for the khata, or VF-6 to see the mutation entries and how the land changed hands.
Select the district, taluka and village.
Enter the survey number or the khata number. If you have neither, search by the owner's name.
Type the verification code and the record opens on screen, in Gujarati.
Print it or save the PDF. This free copy is unsigned and is for your information only.
For a digitally signed copy, register on the site with your mobile number and pay the small fee - this one is accepted where a certified copy is asked for.
For a court case, or where the bank insists on a stamped copy, go to the e-Dhara Kendra at your taluka Mamlatdar office.
If the record shows an old owner after a sale or inheritance, the mutation has not been done - that is a job for the Talati and the e-Dhara Kendra, not the website.
schemes.helpline: e-Dhara Kendra at your taluka Mamlatdar office

schemes.title: e-Nagar - Birth Certificate, Property Tax & Municipal Services
schemes.department: Urban Development & Urban Housing Department, Gujarat
schemes.brief: One login for the municipal work of Gujarat's cities and towns - birth and death certificates, property tax, professional tax, water and drainage connections, shop licences and complaints. Certificates come as digitally signed PDFs you can print at home, so there is no need to stand in a queue for a copy. The portal works in Gujarati and English, and the Civic Centre or Jan Seva Kendra of your municipality will do it for you if you have no computer.
schemes.benefit: Certificates, tax payments and municipal applications without a trip to the office
eligibility: The birth or death must have been registered with a municipality or municipal corporation in Gujarat - village births are registered at the Gram Panchayat instead
For property tax you need the tenement or property number of the property
Anyone can register on the portal with a mobile number
A birth certificate is free if the birth is registered within 21 days; a late fee applies after that
documents: Hospital birth record or the discharge slip, for a first registration
Parents' Aadhaar cards
Address proof
An old property tax bill or receipt showing the tenement number, for tax services
Nothing at all to download a certificate that is already registered - the registration number is enough

demoFields.label: Service chosen
demoFields.value: Birth certificate - download a certified copy
demoFields.hint: Pick the service first. The form changes completely between certificates, tax and connections.

demoFields.label: City or Nagarpalika
demoFields.hint: Choose the body where the birth was registered or where the property is. Choosing the wrong town shows no record.

demoFields.label: Child's name and date of birth
demoFields.hint: If the birth was registered before the child was named, search by date and parents' names instead.

demoFields.label: Registration number
demoFields.hint: From the slip the hospital or the municipality gave at registration. With this the record comes up at once.

demoFields.label: Father's name
demoFields.hint: As given at the time of registration. Used to find the record when you have no registration number.

demoFields.label: Mother's name
demoFields.hint: As given at registration. Both parents' names together narrow the search.

demoFields.label: Tenement / property number
demoFields.hint: For property tax only. It is printed at the top of any old tax bill.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Login is by OTP on this number, and the payment receipt is sent here.

demoFields.label: Amount payable
demoFields.hint: Certificates carry a small fee; property tax shows the dues for the year. Pay by UPI, card or net banking.

demoSteps: Register on e-Nagar with your mobile number and an OTP, or log in if you already have an account.
Switch the language to Gujarati from the top of the page if that is easier.
Choose your municipality or municipal corporation. Everything after this is specific to that town.
For a certificate, open Birth & Death and search by the registration number, or by date of birth with the parents' names.
Check the record on screen carefully - the spelling on the screen is what will print on the certificate.
Pay the small fee online and download the digitally signed PDF. A printout of it is valid; it does not need any further stamp.
For property tax, search by the tenement number, see the dues, pay online and download the receipt at once.
For a new water or drainage connection, or a shop licence, fill the form and upload the papers; the file is then processed by the town's office.
If you have no computer or smartphone, the Civic Centre or Jan Seva Kendra at your municipality does all of this at the counter.
Register a birth within 21 days and the certificate costs nothing - after that a late fee applies and the delay has to be explained.
schemes.helpline: Civic Centre of your municipality or municipal corporation

schemes.title: Ganga Swarupa Yojana - Widow Pension
schemes.department: Women & Child Development Department, Gujarat
schemes.brief: A monthly pension for a widow, paid straight into her bank or post office account. The name of the scheme is deliberate - the government treats her as Ganga Swarupa rather than as a widow. The pension is not stopped when her son turns 21; that old rule has gone. Applications go through e-Samaj Kalyan, but most widows hand the form in at the taluka Mamlatdar's office or a Jan Seva Kendra, and the Talati does the village verification.
schemes.benefit: Rs.1,250 a month, credited by direct transfer
eligibility: Widow aged 18 or above, resident of Gujarat
Family income within the ceiling fixed for rural and for urban areas
Has not remarried - the pension stops on remarriage
Continues even if an adult son lives with her
A continuation certificate has to be given every year for the pension to go on
documents: Husband's death certificate
Widow certificate from the Talati-cum-Mantri or the Mamlatdar
Applicant's Aadhaar card
Income certificate
Age proof - school leaving certificate, birth certificate or an election card
Bank or post office passbook in her own name
Ration card and residence proof

demoFields.label: Applicant's name
demoFields.hint: Her own name as on her Aadhaar card, not her husband's name alone.

demoFields.label: Husband's name and death certificate number
demoFields.hint: The number printed on the death certificate from the Gram Panchayat or Nagarpalika. Nothing moves without this certificate.

demoFields.label: Date of birth / age
demoFields.hint: She must be 18 or above. Give whatever age proof you have - an election card is accepted.

demoFields.label: Aadhaar number
demoFields.hint: Her own Aadhaar, seeded to the account where the pension will come.

demoFields.label: Family annual income
demoFields.hint: From the Mamlatdar's income certificate. The ceiling is different for village and city areas - ask at the Mamlatdar's office which applies to you.

demoFields.label: Bank or post office account and IFSC
demoFields.hint: In her own name only. A post office account is fine. It must be active - a dormant account is the usual reason a pension stops.

demoFields.label: Village / Taluka / District
demoFields.hint: Where she lives. The Talati of this village signs the verification.

demoFields.label: Ration card number
demoFields.hint: From the front of the barcoded ration card, used to establish the family.

demoFields.label: Mobile number
demoFields.hint: Her own or a family member's. The sanction and the monthly credit messages come here.

demoSteps: Collect the husband's death certificate from the Gram Panchayat or Nagarpalika.
Get the widow certificate and the income certificate from the Talati-cum-Mantri and the Mamlatdar's office.
Open a savings account in her own name, at a bank or post office, and get the Aadhaar seeded.
